Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:61: They said: at the time a person departs the world, it is not enough that he is terrified by the Angel of Death, who is entirely full of eyes with his sword drawn in his hand, but he also asks him, "did you occupy yourself with Torah and acts of kindness, and did you proclaim your Maker's sovereignty morning and evening, and did you proclaim your fellow's sovereignty with a pleasant spirit?" If he has these things, he casts that drop into his mouth and his soul departs without pain, like drawing a hair out of milk; but if he does not have these things, his soul departs from his body like dragging thorns out of wool. And when the Angel of Death comes, he says to him, "righteous one, your Maker has sent me to you"; immediately the person entreats him, and he says to him, "this hour cannot be avoided, but I have heard from behind the curtain that the Holy One, blessed be He, is preparing a dwelling for you in the Garden of Eden."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:63: At the time of judgment, the Holy One, blessed be He, says to the person: "I had great trouble over you from when I formed you in your mother's womb, and you were not a miscarriage; and when you came out into the air of the world, I prepared sustenance for you and saved you from sufferings - did you occupy yourself with Torah and perform acts of kindness before Me?" If he has these things, they release him from judgment immediately; if not, he is handed over to five angels of destruction, corresponding to the five books of the Torah - one strikes and one counts, in the manner that they strike and count in a court. A third brings forth fire from his body like a furnace from which fire emerges. The fourth brings bitter and sour herbs from the mountains - if he stole from his fellow, he says to him, "grind with your teeth, for you ate stolen goods with your teeth." The fifth strikes his father and mother, and says to them, "why did you not guide your sons to learn Torah and good deeds, so that he might perform mitzvot and good deeds and separate from evil deeds?" - immediately they are given permission to strike his father and mother; and if he read [Torah] but did not fulfill it, they flog him in their presence - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:64: Although the words of our Sages, of blessed memory, need no reinforcement, and are confirmed of themselves, for their words are with Holy Spirit and are the words of the living God, nevertheless I saw fit to write these lines to arouse those who sleep.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:65: I, the writer, in the year 5330 [1570], in the month of Elul, had come to me in a dream at night a soul from that world, about three months after his passing, and I recognized that he had died, and I asked him about the matters of that world, and he told me at length of the matters of the beating of the grave, and afterward told me that they judge in that world and punish for the precise details of things far more than a person would think in his own mind - and let those who remain hear and fear.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:66: Concerning the judgment of the grave, Rashbi explains (Terumah 151a) that as long as the body remains intact in the grave, the soul is judged in Gehinnom, and after the body decomposes, the soul has rest. And it says: therefore how good it is for them, both for the righteous and for the wicked, that their body cleave to the earth and decompose into dust quickly, and not remain intact for that long a time, so that body and spirit be judged together constantly, every day - for there is not a single righteous person in the world who does not have the judgment of the grave, since that angel appointed over the graves stands over the body and judges it every single day, even for the righteous, so how much more so for the wicked. Therefore, all the time the body decomposes and decays into dust, judgment ceases for it, except for those pious ones present in the world who are fit to have their souls ascend to their Master, to that supernal place fit for them, and they are few in the world - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:67: In the portion of Shelach Lecha (169b) he explains that concerning this it is said (Zechariah 3:3) "and Joshua was clothed in filthy garments" - this being the body of flesh, which is from the side of Samael, of which it is said (Ecclesiastes 4:5; see Zohar there 172b) "the fool folds his hands and eats his own flesh." And as long as the body, which is from the side of Samael, remains intact, they do not clothe the soul with the garment fit for it in the Garden of Eden; only after the flesh decomposes do they clothe it with its garment - this is (Zechariah 3:4-5) "remove the filthy garments from upon him," etc., "and they clothed him with garments, and the angel of the Lord stood" - for from the Shechinah, called "the angel of the Lord," the soul is given its garment. Therefore a person must diminish the flesh, which is from the kelipah, and increase the repair of the garment of his soul, which stands and endures forever, for the world that is entirely long.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:1: <small>In the explanation of the particular sins for which one is punished in Gehinnom, as found written in the Zohar and the midrashim, and the nature of Gehinnom.</small>
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:2: The fire of Gehinnom, our Sages, of blessed memory, explain (Chagigah 13b), flows from the river of fire [Nehar Dinur] - their words: "'behold, the storm of the Lord, wrath, has gone forth' - this is the river of fire. From where does it come forth? Rabbi Yirmiyah bar Abba said, from the sweat of the Chayot. And where does it pour out? Rav Chilkiyah bar Tuvi said, upon the heads of the wicked in Gehinnom, as it is said (Jeremiah 23:19) 'behold, the storm of the Lord, wrath, has gone forth, a whirling storm; it shall burst upon the head of the wicked'" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:3: Further, the matter of Gehinnom was revealed to us by Isaiah the prophet, when he said (Isaiah 30:33) "for a hearth [Tophet] has already been prepared, it too is prepared for the king; He has made it deep and wide, its pyre has much fire and wood," etc. And further, near this prophecy, he says (ibid. 31:9) "says the Lord, whose fire is in Zion and whose furnace is in Jerusalem." And our Sages, of blessed memory, explain in Midrash Aggadat Shmuel (Pesikta Rabbati, chapter 41), on the verse "for a hearth has already been prepared," etc., "He has made it deep and wide" - Rabbi Pinchas and Rabbi Chonya said, since the wicked say, "how many tens of thousands can Gehinnom hold - two hundred myriads, three hundred myriads? How many wicked people are there in every generation?" - the Holy One, blessed be He, said, "however many you increase in the world, it too widens and deepens every day," as it is said, "for a hearth has already been prepared," etc. - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:4: In the Zohar (Terumah 150b), this matter is explained, saying that the fire of Gehinnom burns only through the wicked heating themselves in the fire of their own inclination - his words: "Rabbi Yehudah said: the judgment of the punishments of Gehinnom - we have learned that it is to judge the wicked there. On what are they judged in the fire of Gehinnom? Rather, Gehinnom is a fire burning day and night, and just as the wicked heat themselves in the fire of the evil inclination to transgress the words of the Torah, so with every heating by which they heat themselves with the evil inclination, so is the fire of Gehinnom kindled."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:5: Once, the evil inclination was not found in the world, because it was placed inside an iron seal in the hole of the great deep, and all that time the fire of Gehinnom went out and did not burn at all. The evil inclination returned to its place, the wicked of the world began to warm themselves with it, and the fire of Gehinnom began to burn, for Gehinnom burns only from the heat of the strength of the wicked's evil inclination, and by that heat Gehinnom burns day and night and does not subside.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:6: There are seven gates to Gehinnom, and seven chambers there, and seven kinds of wicked - evil [ra], worthless [beliya'al], sinner [chotei], wicked [rasha], destroyer [mashchit], scorner [letz], and arrogant [yahir] - and corresponding to each of them there are chambers in Gehinnom, each fitting its kind, and according to the level at which that wicked one sinned, so is he given a chamber in Gehinnom; and in every single chamber there is an angel appointed over that place, under the hand of Dumah, and how many thousands and myriads are with him, who judge the wicked, each according to what fits him in that chamber where he is.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:7: The fire of Gehinnom below reaches from within the fire of Gehinnom above, and reaches that Gehinnom below, and burns from that arousal of the heat of the wicked, who warm themselves within the evil inclination, and all those chambers burn there - so far. And it says that the fire of Gehinnom below comes from within the fire of Gehinnom above - the secret of the Gehinnom above is the river of fire in which souls are refined, as is explained in the portion of Vayakhel, as we shall quote further; and that river of fire descends into the Gehinnom on earth, as our Sages, of blessed memory, explain it has three gates, and the wicked, through their own heat, cause the fire of the supernal river of fire to be drawn down below.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:8: Concerning the three gates that Gehinnom has, our Sages, of blessed memory, said in Eruvin (19a) - their words: "Rabbi Yirmiyah said in the name of Rabbi Elazar, Gehinnom has three gates - one in the wilderness, one in the sea, and one in Jerusalem. In the wilderness, as it is written (Numbers 16:33) 'and they went down, they and all that belonged to them, alive, into Sheol.' In the sea, as it is written (Jonah 2:3) 'out of the belly of Sheol I cried.' In Jerusalem, as it is written (Isaiah 31:9) 'whose fire is in Zion and whose furnace is in Jerusalem,' and it was taught in the school of Rabbi Yishmael, 'whose fire is in Zion' - this is the entrance to Gehinnom." And is there no more? But is there not that which Rabbi Miryon said in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, and some say it was taught by Rav Mari son of Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai: there are two date palms in the Valley of Ben Hinnom, and smoke rises between them, and this is what we learned, "the fig trees of the Iron Mountain are fit [for a certain use]," and this is the entrance to Gehinnom - perhaps this is the same as the one in the wilderness.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:9: And to the wicked person who denies the matter of Gehinnom, we say to him: let him go to the wilderness, there to the crevices of Korach, as they said in Bava Batra (74a), in the stories of Rabbah bar Bar Chana: he said to me, "come, I will show you the swallowed ones of Korach." I saw two crevices from which smoke was rising; I took a tuft of wool, soaked it in water, and stuck it on the head of a spear, and inserted it there, and when I took it out, it was scorched. He said to me, "listen, what do you hear?" And I heard them saying, "Moses is true and his Torah is true, and they [Korach and his company] are liars." He said to me, "every thirty days Gehinnom turns them back here like meat in a pot, and they say thus: Moses is true and his Torah is true, and they are liars" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:10: Further, the matter of Gehinnom has been confirmed through several stories that occurred in our generation, and our forefathers likewise told us, but we shall not lengthen, so as not to stray from the intended purpose.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:11: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said (there, in Eruvin): Gehinnom has seven names, and these are they: Sheol, Avaddon, Be'er Shachat, Bor Sha'on, Tit HaYaven, Tzalmavet, and Eretz Tachtit. "Sheol," as it is written (Jonah 2:3) "out of the belly of Sheol I cried." "Avaddon," as it is written (Psalms 88:12) "shall Your kindness be told in the grave, Your faithfulness in Avaddon?" "Be'er Shachat" [Pit of Destruction], as it is written (ibid. 55:24) "but You, O God, shall bring them down to the pit of destruction." "Bor Sha'on" [Roaring Pit] and "Tit HaYaven" [Miry Clay], as it is written (ibid. 40:3) "and He brought me up out of the roaring pit, out of the miry clay," etc. "Tzalmavet" [Shadow of Death], as it is written (ibid. 107:10) "those who dwell in darkness and the shadow of death." "Eretz Tachtit" [Lowest Land] - from the Talmud [i.e., an established term].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:12: And is there not also "Gehinnom"? A valley as deep as the Valley of Hinnom. Another interpretation: whoever descends into it descends on account of "hinnam" [gratuitous/wanton] matters. And is there not also "Tophet"? As it is said (Isaiah 30:33) "for a Tophet has already been prepared" - that whoever is enticed [mitpateh] by his inclination falls there - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:13: Further, they say in the midrash (Pesikta Rabbati, chapter 41): "for behold, those who are far from You shall perish" (Psalms 73:27) - David said, since whoever is far from You in this world is lost for the World to Come. "You have cut off all who go astray [zoneh] from You" - the wicked, who condemn themselves through their sins and estrange themselves from You, so too, what do You do to them? You condemn them to Gehinnom; and "tzamatah" [cut off] denotes finality, as it is said (Leviticus 25:30) "in finality [latzemitut] to him who bought it" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:14: Since we have spoken of the matter of Gehinnom, I have chosen to copy here "Masechet Gehinnom" [Tractate Gehinnom], which I found among the words of our Sages, of blessed memory, in manuscript.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:16: It is written (Nahum 1:6) "before His indignation, who can stand, and who can rise up in the fierceness of His anger?" Rabbi Ze'eira opened, "the leech has two daughters, Give, Give" (Proverbs 30:15) - Rabbi Elazar said, two companies of angels stand at the gates of Gehinnom and say, "Give, Give," "Bring, Bring." And why is it called Gehinnom? Because its roar travels from one end of the world to the other. And why is it called Tophet? Because everyone enters it through the enticement [pituy] of the evil inclination.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:18: Rabbi Yochanan opened (Psalms 84:7) "passing through the valley of weeping, they make it a place of springs, also the early rain covers it with blessings [or: covers it as a teacher]" - this teaches that the wicked person confesses, just as the leper confesses, and says, "I, so-and-so, son of so-and-so, committed such-and-such a transgression in such-and-such a place, on such-and-such a day, before so-and-so, in the presence of so-and-so and so-and-so."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:19: There are three gates in Gehinnom, one in the sea, one in the wilderness, and one in inhabited land. This one in the sea - from where do we derive it? As it is said (Jonah 2:3) "out of the belly of Sheol I cried, You heard my voice." This one in the wilderness - from where do we derive it? As it is said (Numbers 16:33) "and they went down, they and all that belonged to them, alive, into Sheol." This one in inhabited land - as it is said (Isaiah 31:9) "says the Lord, whose fire is in Zion and whose furnace is in Jerusalem."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:20: There are five kinds of fire in Gehinnom: fire that eats and drinks, that drinks and does not eat, that eats and does not drink, that neither eats nor drinks, and there is fire that eats fire. There are coals in it like mountains, and coals in it like hills, and coals in it like the Dead Sea, and coals in it like great stones; there are rivers of pitch and sulfur in it, flowing and boiling, in waves upon waves.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:21: The sentence of a wicked person: angels of destruction push him on his face, and others receive him from them and push him before the fire of Gehinnom, and it opens its mouth and swallows him, as it is said (Isaiah 5:14) "therefore Sheol has enlarged its desire and opened its mouth without limit, and their glory, their multitude, their tumult, and he who rejoices in it, shall go down into it" - this applies to one who has not a single mitzvah to tip the scale to the side of merit; but whoever has Torah and good deeds and many sufferings come upon him is saved from the judgment of Gehinnom, as it is said (Psalms 23:4) "even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for You are with me; Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me" - "Your rod" refers to sufferings, and "Your staff" refers to Torah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:23: Rabbi Yochanan opened (Job 11:20) "but the eyes of the wicked shall fail, and their refuge shall perish, and their hope shall be the giving up of the ghost" - a body that does not perish, and a soul that departs by a fire that is not quenched, and of them Scripture says (Isaiah 66:24) "for their worm shall not die, nor their fire be quenched."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:24: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: once I was walking on the road, and Elijah the prophet, remembered for good, found me. He said to me, "do you wish that I set you at the gate of Gehinnom?" I said to him, "yes." He showed me people hanging by their noses, and people hanging by their hands, and people hanging by their tongues, and people hanging by their feet; and he showed me women hanging by their breasts; and he showed me people hanging by their eyes; and he showed me people whom they feed with their own flesh, and people whom they feed with burning coals of broom-wood; and people sitting alive while worms devour them - he said to me, "these are they of whom it is written, 'for their worm shall not die.'" And he showed me people whom they feed with fine sand, and they forced them to eat it and their teeth broke, and the Holy One, blessed be He, says to them, "wicked ones, when you ate stolen goods it was sweet in your mouths, and now you have no strength to eat," to fulfill what is said (Psalms 3:8) "You have broken the teeth of the wicked."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:25: And he showed me people whom they cast from fire to snow and from snow to fire, like a shepherd who pastures his flock from mountain to mountain, and of them Scripture says (Psalms 49:15) "like sheep they are laid in Sheol; death shall be their shepherd, and the upright shall have dominion over them in the morning; and their form shall be for Sheol to consume, that there be no dwelling for it."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:26: Rabbi Yochanan said: every single angel is appointed to exact the punishment for one transgression - this one comes and judges him and goes his way, and so the second and so the third and so all of them, until they complete all the transgressions in his hand. To what can this be compared? To a debtor who had many creditors, and they brought him before the king; the king said to them, "what shall I do for you? Go and divide him among yourselves." At that hour his soul is delivered in Gehinnom to cruel angels, and they divide it among themselves.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:28: It is taught: three go down to Gehinnom and do not come up - one who has relations with a married woman, one who shames his fellow publicly, and one who swears falsely by the Name of the Lord; and some say, also one who glorifies himself through his fellow's disgrace, and one who incites strife between a man and his wife to bring discord between them. Every Friday afternoon they are brought to two mountains of snow and left there, and at the conclusion of the Sabbath they are returned to their place, and an angel comes forth and pushes them and returns them to their place in Gehinnom; and from that [snow] they take some and place it under their armpits to cool themselves during the six weekdays. And the Holy One, blessed be He, says to them, "wicked ones, woe to you, for even in Gehinnom you steal," as it is said (Job 24:19) "drought and heat consume the snow waters, so does Sheol those who have sinned" - meaning, even in Sheol they sin.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:30: Every twelve months they are made into ashes, and the wind scatters them beneath the feet of the righteous, as it is written (Malachi 3:21) "and you shall trample the wicked, for they shall be ashes under the soles of your feet"; and afterward their souls return to them, and they go out of Gehinnom with their faces black as the bottom of a pot, and they justify the judgment upon themselves and say, "You have decreed rightly upon us, You have judged us rightly; to You, O Lord, belongs the righteousness, and to us the shame of face, as at this day."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:31: But the nations of the world, worshipers of idolatry, are judged in seven chambers of fire, twelve months in each and every chamber, and a river of fire goes forth from beneath the Throne of Glory and descends upon them, traveling from one end of the world to the other.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:32: There are seven chambers in Gehinnom, and in each and every chamber there are six thousand houses, and in each and every house there are six thousand windows, and in each and every window there are six thousand jars of gall, and they are all ready for the recorders and the judges; and concerning that hour Solomon said, "and I shall be found clean in the end." And not one of them escapes unless he has Torah and good deeds.
